text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG

- Junior coalition partners the Free Democrats (FDP) want to steadfastly stick to their policy of a reduction in the "solidarity tax" -- the surcharge introduced to finance development in east Germany -- and their opposition to any tax hikes, ahead of their party congress later this week.
- Authorities for the civil service alternative to military service say fewer young men are refusing to do their time in the army and opting for civil service.
- Chancellor Helmut Kohl set to launch joint initiative for more jobs in eastern Germany on Thursday.
- Germany's largest bank Deutsche Bank AG is set for another year of record results.
- The Munich Ifo economic institute warns against getting up false hopes that the introduction of the European single currency will significantly reduce unemployment.
HANDELSBLATT
- Deutsche Bank AG's outgoing chief executive Hilmar Kopper leaves his successor Rolf Breuer a golden balance sheet.

- German federation of employers' (BDA) president Dieter Hundt praises head of German Federation of Trade Unions (DGB) Dieter Schulte for saying that a reduction in pension levels was unavoidable given demographic developments.
- Unions and employers set to agree to a new initiative to create an annual 100,000 new jobs in east Germany.

- Munich Ifo economic institute says investment in east German industry is not declining as quickly as had been thought and could sink five percent -- not an expected 15 percent -- to 16.2 billion marks this year.
- German retail group Metro AG announces takeover of rival PC retailer Peacock AG and Peacock Systeme GmbH.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG

- Comments by the DGB's Schulte over pension reform are widely supported and set off a row in the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) whose pension commission had recommended a rejection of any cuts to pension levels.
- FDP budget expert Juergen Koppelin says the acquisition of Eurofighter jets is not affordable at the moment.
- Finance Minister Theo Waigel wants to reform budget law so ministerial departments have more rights and responsibilities over their budgets.
- Outgoing Deutsche Bank chief executive Kopper hands over control of the bank to Breuer.
- Justice Minister Edzard Schmitz-Jortzig wants to make the decision of the individual whether to donate their organs in the case of death a legal obligation.
DIE WELT
- The federal government, unions, east German states and leading industry associations surprise by agreeing to a joing initiative to create more 100,000 new jobs each year in eastern Germany.
- Junior coalition partners the FDP stick by opposition to tax hikes ahead of their party congress at the end of the week.
- SPD premiers of Schleswig-Holstein and North Rhine-Westphalia Heide Simonis and Johannes Rau call on companies to invest in innovation at the beginning of the SPD innovation congress.
